tldr: Additive treatment-effect models retain interpretable nonconstant main effects while excluding interactions. Under public uniform product covariates, binary original records, Hölder-\(1/8\) assignment and baseline regressions, and a contrast with Lipschitz gradient, the central question asks for a finite-uniform full-additive-null testing frontier. The proved unknown-propensity frontier is \(n^{-4/21}\), the proved supplied-propensity frontier and fixed-smoothness dense Gaussian additivity benchmark order are \(n^{-2/5}\), and the resulting penalty ratio is \(n^{22/105}\). The binary causal upper bounds and all-procedure converses match with finite constants, and no logarithmic factor is necessary. Crump--Hotz--Imbens--Mitnik is the primary published causal comparator: its asymptotic constant-CATE tests address a strict subnull within this model. Chang--Lee--Whang and Hsu supply asymptotic conditional-effect tests for their own equality or inequality nulls; Dai--Shen--Stern supplies observational finite-strata tests. These results are different theorem targets, not results claimed to be strictly improved. Dhawan--Guo--Shah occupies the general weighted null-space projection. Functional corrected-score profiling and zero-marginal full-support binary mixtures are the handles, with substantial credit to internal constant-null machinery. The contribution is incremental and field-level, with the general projection transfer credited and the source limits disclosed.
